findings.message: The three deleted lines are the defect itself, not coverage: an import widened and two duplicated os-native renderings replaced by one seam. No assertion, fixture or platform guard was removed.
findings.detail_md:
Deletions, read in full: `from pathlib import Path` (widened to `Path, PurePath, PureWindowsPath`) and the same statement twice, `rel = md_path.relative_to(repo_root)` — the two divergent call sites that rendered a violation's `file:line` prefix with the host's native separator. Both now call one `_posix_relpath` seam returning `relative_to(...).as_posix()`, so the enforcer compares one canonical form instead of two host-dependent ones. Two call sites collapsed into one is the shape the standing order asks for: the Windows red was a duplication defect, and the fix removes the duplication rather than special-casing the platform.

The new `test_posix_relpath_is_separator_agnostic_under_windows_path_semantics` drives the seam with `PureWindowsPath(r"D:\\...")` inputs and asserts the rendered path is POSIX-shaped with no backslash. Because `relative_to`/`as_posix` are pure path arithmetic with no I/O, that test exercises Windows semantics **on every host** — no `skipif`, so the regression cannot hide until the next Windows CI run.

Security-relevant check: `as_posix()` on a `relative_to` result is separator normalisation only — it neither collapses `..` segments nor resolves symlinks, so the enforcer's path matching is not loosened. The ledger carries `reported` (HIGH, project-manager) and `resolved` (software-engineer) with all three FR23 fields and an honestly-argued `net-neutral:` direction that distinguishes raw LOC from defect-bearing logic.
